newsitem.title: USA: Cominco set '97 lead concentrate benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Cominco set '97 lead concentrate benchmark.

text.p: Cominco Ltd settled its lead concentrates treatment charge benchmark deal for 1997 at $177 per tonne with a London Metal Exchange lead cash basis price of $600 per tonne, a source at the company said.
The deal represents a slight shift in favor of smelters, with an treatment charge hike of $1 to $2 per tonne above last year's settlement of $175 per tonne, on a similar LME cash price basis.
The company source said the deal covered close to 60,000 tonnes of lead concentrates.
Wednesday, Cominco and Metaleurop concluded their 1997 benchmark deal for zinc concentrates at a treatment charge of $186 a tonne basis LME cash price of $1,100 a tonne.
If the $186 treatment charge was reevaluated on an LME base price of $1,000 a tonne, it equates to $170, the Cominco source noted. "This is a $20 cut in favor of the miners this year," he added.
In 1996, the zinc treatment charge was settled at $190 basis LME $1,000.
The Cominco official said he was pleased with the acceptance of greater price participation between smelters and miners in this year's zinc treatment charge.

Cominco offered an escalator of 20 cents, up five cents from last year, and a much bigger deescalator of 15 cents. The company sought to graft such a change onto TC deals to give smelters an incentive to cut output when zinc prices fell.
In the past, miners suffered most from any dip in zinc prices while smelters continued to produce at capacity.

But with zinc tags widely seen as remaining firm or even strengthening this year, the acceptance by smelters of a much higher deescalators in 1997 deals was largely symbolic, industry executives said.
Nevertheless, with higher escalators, smelters will profit more from the stronger zinc prices, and this was Cominco's carrot for smelters to accept a lower base TC this year.
But the challenge for the miners will be to include a high deescalators in a year when the zinc price is forecast to fall.
